known_facts_book1: Opens the book sitting on a bank beside her sister, bored by her sister's book because it has no pictures or conversations.
Follows the White Rabbit down the rabbit-hole after seeing it take a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket.
Falls past cupboards, bookshelves, maps and pictures, and takes an empty marmalade jar off a shelf as she falls.
Finds a tiny golden key on a three-legged glass table that opens a small door onto a garden she is too large to enter.
Drinks from a bottle labelled 'DRINK ME' and shrinks to ten inches high, then eats a cake marked 'EAT ME'.
Says 'Curiouser and curiouser!' when she grows.
Swims in a pool of her own tears and offends the Mouse by talking about Dinah and about a terrier that catches mice.
Is mistaken by the White Rabbit for his housemaid Mary Ann and sent to fetch his gloves and fan.
Grows too big for the White Rabbit's house, filling it with one arm out of the window and one foot up the chimney.
Recites 'You are old, Father William' to the Caterpillar and gets the words wrong.
Uses the two sides of the Caterpillar's mushroom to change size, at one point stretching her neck above the treetops.
Is accused by the Pigeon of being a serpent after eggs.
Nurses the Duchess's baby out of the kitchen and it turns into a pig, which she sets down and lets run into the wood.
Sits down uninvited in a large arm-chair at the tea party after the March Hare and the Hatter cry 'No room!'
Leaves the tea party in disgust; the last she sees of them, they are trying to put the Dormouse into the teapot.
Finds three gardeners painting white roses red and asks them, a little timidly, why they are doing it.
Hides the three gardeners in a large flower-pot to save them from the Queen's soldiers.
Refuses to lie down on her face when the royal procession arrives.
Introduces the Cheshire Cat to the King as 'a friend of mine'.
Plays croquet with a flamingo for a mallet and a hedgehog for a ball.
Wonders whether the pepper in the kitchen was what made the Duchess so savage.
Tells the Mock Turtle she has never lived under the sea, never been introduced to a lobster, and never tasted one.
Has read about courts of justice in books and is pleased to know the name of nearly everything in the courtroom.
Is proud of knowing the word 'jurors', reflecting that very few girls of her age would know its meaning.
Grows during the trial until she upsets the jury-box with her skirt and tips the jurymen into the crowd.
Declares the court 'nothing but a pack of cards' and wakes on the bank with her head in her sister's lap.
The whole of Wonderland turns out to have been her dream; her sister sits on afterwards thinking of it.

known_relations_book1.White Rabbit: The creature she follows into Wonderland; it mistakes her for its housemaid Mary Ann and later acts as herald at the trial. No friendship — it is frightened of her and scurries away.
known_relations_book1.Dinah: Her own pet cat, left at home and repeatedly missed; mentioning Dinah is what offends the Mouse and scatters the birds.
known_relations_book1.Cheshire Cat: The one creature she calls a friend; she introduces it to the King and values it as 'somebody to talk to'.
known_relations_book1.Queen: Adversary. The Queen orders her execution for insolence and Alice contradicts her loudly and decidedly.
known_relations_book1.King: Presides over the trial as judge and questions her; he is mild where the Queen is violent, and reminds the Queen that Alice is only a child.
known_relations_book1.Caterpillar: Interrogates her with 'Who are you?', makes her recite a poem, and finally tells her which side of the mushroom does what.
known_relations_book1.Duchess: Meets her twice — savage in the kitchen, affectionate on the croquet-ground, and relentlessly moralising the second time.
known_relations_book1.the Mouse: The first creature she speaks to in Wonderland; she offends it twice by talking about cats and dogs.
known_relations_book1.Gryphon: Takes her to the Mock Turtle by the Queen's order and tells her the Queen's executions never happen.
known_relations_book1.Mock Turtle: Tells her his history and the Lobster Quadrille; she listens and admits she knows nothing of the sea.
known_relations_book1.Hatter: Meets him at the mad tea party, is offended by his personal remarks and his unanswerable riddle.
